thread.title: Bull trend pauses: S&P 500 holds the breakout point (2,916) ahead of the Fed - MarketWatch

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Bull trend pauses: S&P 500 holds the breakout point (2,916) ahead of the Fed - MarketWatch
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Though the bigger-picture backdrop is not one-size-fits-all, the major U.S. benchmarks are acting well technically ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy statement, due out Wednesday.
Consider that the S&P 500 has maintained its breakout point (2,916) — surviving this week’s initial retest — while the Dow industrials continue to digest a powerful September spike to uncharted territory.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, -0.01% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
As illustrated, the S&P has maintained its breakout point (2,916) an area defined by the August peak. The price action is constructive, though the retest remains underway.
Similarly, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has pulled in modestly from record territory.
Tactically, the January peak (26,616) remains an inflection point, and is followed by deeper gap support (26,464).
More broadly, the steep late-month breakout, and comparably flat pullback, signal that selling pressure near record territory remains muted.
True to recent form, the Nasdaq Composite continues to lag behind.
As illustrated, the index remains capped by the familiar range top (8,042).
Conversely, the July peak (7,933) closely matches key trendline support, an area better illustrated below.
Widening the view to six months adds perspective.
On this wider view, the Nasdaq has maintained trendline support, an area currently matching the July peak (7,933). The slightly deeper 50-day moving average, currently 7,899, closely tracks the trendline.
Conversely, near-term resistance (8,042) has effectively capped the September range.
Tactically, price action within the prevailing range supports a bullish intermediate-term bias. Still, the pending break from the range will likely add color.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has taken flight.
The chart above includes the 20-day Bollinger bands, also known as volatility bands. Illustrated in red, the bands encompass two standard deviations of the Dow’s trailing 20-day volatility.
As always, consecutive closes atop the bands are statistically unusual, and signal a tension between two time horizons.
For the near-term, the index is overbought and due to consolidate. The breakout has placed the index up on a stilt, outside the trailing two standard deviation band.
But more importantly, the underlying bullish momentum has registered as extreme, likely laying the groundwork for longer-term upside follow-through.
In the current case, the Dow has notched three straight closes atop the bands, a stretch that was snapped Monday.
Moreover, the Dow also notched consecutive session lows atop the bands, an unusual event for an index. To reiterate, a breakout of this magnitude might be expected from a name like Tilray, though not so much from the Dow industrials.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has broken out less decisively, notching a single close atop the volatility bands (not illustrated) last week.
Tactically, initial support matches the breakout point (2,916) and is followed by the 20-day moving average, currently 2,900.
The bigger picture The U.S. benchmarks are setting up well for a strong year-end with the third quarter set to conclude this week.
Still, the immediate backdrop is not one-size-fits-all.
On a headline basis, the Dow industrials have taken flight — staging a powerful break to record territory — while the Nasdaq Composite has established a September holding pattern, underpinned by trendline support.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF has flatlined at major support.
The specific area matches the breakout point (170.20) and is closely followed by the 50-day moving average, currently 169.10.
Meanwhile, the SPDR S&P MidCap 400 is digesting a more decisive August break to record territory.
Its orderly one-month range is underpinned by the breakout point (366.70) and trendline support.
Against this backdrop, Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP, -0.13% has rallied decisively to record territory.
As its name suggests, the RSP assigns an equal weight to the S&P’s 500 components, removing the disproportionate influence of mega-caps, including for instance Apple, Amazon and Alphabet.
Notably, the September breakout has registered as powerful, encompassing two straight closes atop the 20-day volatility bands last week. To reiterate, consecutive closes atop the bands are statistically unusual, and distinctly bullish for the longer-term.
Perhaps more usefully, the breakout contradicts a recently popular bear-case contention that the prevailing rally is precariously narrow.
Placing a finer point on the S&P 500, its six-month backdrop remains straightforward.
Tactically, well-defined support matches the breakout point (2,916) an area the S&P has initially maintained.
Delving deeper, a firmer floor matches the breakout point, an area broadly spanning from 2,863 to 2,873. The 50-day moving average, currently 2,862, is rising toward the breakout point, and the S&P’s intermediate-term bias remains bullish barring a violation.
Beyond specific levels, the response to the Federal Reserve’s policy statement, due out Wednesday, and Friday’s third-quarter close will likely add color.
See also: Charting a bull-flag breakout attempt: Dow industrials challenge seven-month highs.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Drilling down further, the 10-year Treasury note yield TNX, +0.78% has broken out, rising to challenge seven-year highs.
The upturn precedes Wednesday’s FOMC policy statement, including a widely-expected interest-rate hike.
Technically, the prevailing breakout resolves a double bottom — defined by the July and August lows — and has also has filled the May gap.
Last-ditch resistance matches the May peak (3.115) while an intermediate-term target projects from the double bottom to the 3.21 area. Much more broadly, the yield’s next notable overhead broadly spans from about 3.60 to 3.74, an area defining the 2011 peak.
Meanwhile, the United States Oil Fund USO, +0.13% has come to life, rising to challenge 34-month highs. The fund tracks the price of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) light, sweet crude oil.
Technically, the shares are challenging 34-month highs, an area matching trendline resistance and the July peak (15.25).
A breakout opens the path to much less-charted territory — illustrated on the four-year chart — and potentially material longer-term follow-through. An intermediate-term target projects to the 17.10 area.
More broadly, rising oil prices and interest rates — as detailed above — might conventionally present a stock market headwind. Still, the tandem resurgence is constructive to the extent it reflects a reflation trade, consistent with a strengthening economy.
Moving to U.S. sectors, the Energy Select Sector SPDR has come to life, rising amid crude oil’s breakout attempt. (Yield = 2.7%.)
As illustrated, the group has cleared trendline resistance, reaching eight-week highs.
The upturn resolves a mini double bottom — underpinned by the 200-day moving average — and signals an intermediate-term trend shift.
Tactically, the trendline pivots to support, and is followed by the former range bottom, circa 73.50. The group’s intermediate-term bias remains bullish barring a violation. More broadly, the group is also well positioned on the four-year chart.
Moving to specific names, FireEye, Inc. FEYE, +4.00% is a mid-cap cybersecurity name coming to life.
As illustrated, the shares have rallied atop trendline resistance, reaching two-month highs. The strong-volume breakout signals a trend shift.
Tactically, the trendline pivots to support — an area roughly matching the 200-day moving average — and the rally attempt is intact barring a violation.
Teladoc, Inc. TDOC, +3.25% is a mid-cap provider of virtual health services.
Technically, the shares have established a tight one-month range, digesting the August rally to record territory.
The range bottom closely matches the 50-day moving average — a level that has defined the prevailing uptrend — and a breakout attempt is in play barring a violation. A near-term target projects to the 85.50 area on follow-through.
Initially profiled Oct. 4, HubSpot, Inc. HUBS, +1.54% has returned 75.4% and remains well positioned.
Earlier this month, the shares knifed to record territory, rising sharply atop resistance matching the June peak.
The subsequent pullback has been comparably flat, placing the shares at an attractive entry near the breakout point (143) and 8.8% under the September peak. Delving slightly deeper, the 50-day moving average, currently 138.20, has marked a recent inflection point.
